The first war broadcast live with Graded in action. CNN and Spotlight crews film Aurelian Defense heroes and Army Graded clearing Iraqi positions. Graded enlistment triples. Aurelian Defense Solutions is born on the back of the contracts.
PARAGON (Gil Haverkamp, 1951-1991): the Pinnacle's founding leader, A-V COR (flight, strength, durability), and America's hero for eight years. He dies in Kuwait in February 1991, killed by a coordinated Iraqi Graded ambush, during a mission Aurelian scheduled for the cameras. His funeral is the most-watched broadcast of the year, and Aurelian sells memorial merchandise within a week.
Private truth: Paragon was synthetic (one of Aurelian's first Ichor successes, in 1975), and he was openly drinking and burning out by 1990. Aurelian's internal memos called the Kuwait mission a "legacy opportunity."
Gulf War Graded veterans return with Strain injuries and "Gulf Syndrome." The VA denies their claims for years.

87.comment: The Foundry Riots and Calvin Merritt
87.content:
[GRADED: The Foundry Riots (1992)]
March 1991: Calvin Merritt, 26, a D-Rank COR bike courier with a Utility license, is pulled over in Port Harlan. Four PHPD officers beat him for nine minutes while he stays on the ground without using his power. A neighbor films it on a camcorder.
April 1992: an all-baseline jury in Kesler Heights acquits the officers ("reasonable fear of an Enhanced suspect"). The Old Foundry erupts. Three days of riots follow: 31 dead, and $300M in damage. Graded rioters fight National Guard troops, Pinnacle heroes are deployed against residents, and Graded-owned and baseline-owned businesses alike burn.
Aftermath: Merritt pleads on TV for calm. The officers are later convicted on federal charges. The riots shape the Old Foundry for a generation and give birth to the Graded rights movement that becomes Equal Ground. Many '70s-born Graded in Port Harlan were teenagers or young adults in the streets those three days.

88.content:
[GRADED: The Hollow Creek Siege (1993)]
Hollow Creek, Texas: a religious community called the Children of the Upward Light, led by "Brother Amos" (Amos Kerrigan, a B-Rank PSI empath who told followers his power was divine).
February 1993: a Bureau raid over weapons and unregistered Graded goes wrong. Four agents and six members die. Then a 51-day standoff: Bureau Sniffers report that Amos is using his empathy on everyone inside, and negotiators complain of "feeling his despair" through the walls. On day 51, during a gas assault, the compound burns. 76 die, including 25 children. Who started the fire is still disputed.
Aftermath: Congressional hearings and a surge in anti-government militia movements. The Ascension Church (founded in 1997) honors the Hollow Creek dead as "the first martyrs," and Flatline's founders cite it as proof the Bureau can't handle the Graded.

89.content:
[GRADED: The Ghostline Trial (1995)]
Ray Dorsey, "Ghostline," a B-IV SPA (phasing) member of the Pinnacle since 1983 and a beloved national star, is charged with murdering his ex-wife, Laura Dorsey (a baseline), and her friend in their locked Kesler Heights home. The prosecution: only someone who can phase through walls could have done it. The defense: other SPA Graded exist, the Bureau's Sniffer evidence was mishandled, and the police hated Graded.
A 9-month televised trial; Aurelian quietly funds his defense. October 1995: acquittal. Baseline America is furious; many Graded celebrate, seeing a verdict against police bias. Aurelian drops him from the Pinnacle within a month anyway.
He lives quietly in the Ashgrove hills, 70 years old by 2026, and still insists he's innocent. The question "did Ghostline do it" still splits families at dinner tables.

90.content:
[GRADED: 1999]
THE CHICAGO FLARE (June 1999): OVERCAST (Dana Whitlow, 31), an S-Rank KIN (storm and pressure) hero under a city contract, is pushed by her sponsor through back-to-back events and a tornado-season emergency. Her Strain hits 100% during a public rally in the Loop. The Flare levels six blocks and kills 2,300, including Overcast. Strain science becomes front-page news overnight: every network airs "Strain explained" specials, and Congress funds the research that leads to Quell (2003).
Y2K: fear that computers will fail at midnight on January 1, 2000. Corporations and the government hire TEC Graded at enormous fees to audit code. Nothing happens. TEC Graded claim credit; baselines call it a scam. Either way, the TEC Graded get rich.

91.content:
[GRADED: Pinnacle Lineups]
1983 founding lineup: PARAGON (A-V COR, leader, died 1991) · LADY VOLT (Ruth Ann Kowalski, B-III KIN electric; retired 1994; 79 in 2026, in a Florida retirement home with Inversion symptoms) · MIRAGE (Norvell Price, B-IV PSI illusion; quit in 1986 during the Psi Panic, now a reclusive painter) · TIDEWATER (Carla Mendes, A-III MAT water; Faded out in 2001; now an Aurelian board member) · LONGSHOT (Jim Barlow, C-V PER marksman; killed in 1988, officially in action, though rumor says Flatline's precursors did it) · GHOSTLINE (Ray Dorsey, B-IV SPA; dropped in 1995).
1990s: after Paragon's death, Tidewater leads; new members cycle through faster as the Pinnacle becomes a TV product. Bulwark joins in 1998.
2000s-2020s: Meridian (2006), Echo (2011), Cecile (2018), Jackknife (2020), and Gridlock (2024) join. Over the years, 14 former members have died: 5 in action, 4 by Flare or Strain, 3 by suicide, and 2 of "unknown" causes.

92.content:
[GRADED: Port Harlan by Decade]
1970s: a declining port and steel town. Aurelian's 1972 move brings money to downtown, which is still called the "Exchange District" (renamed the Spire after 1994). Riverside has union docks and the mob. The Old Foundry is still a working-class steel neighborhood, mostly baseline. Kesler Heights is new postwar suburbs.
1980s: the mills close (1979-83). Graded families, priced and pushed out of everywhere else, move into the Foundry's empty tenements. Crack and Burn arrive; Pinnacle billboards go up downtown; Ashgrove grows rich.
1990s: the Foundry Riots (1992). Aurelian Tower is built (1994). The Exchange District becomes "the Spire," and gentrification starts pushing poorer residents toward Riverside. Kesler Heights booms with white-flight and baseline-flight families. The Choir starts as a small Riverside crew.
2000s-2020s: Quell policing, then Rush. The Low Kings form (2011), the Spire turns luxury, and the Foundry stays poor and proud.

93.content:
[GRADED: The World]
The Halden scale (F to X, Grades I to V, the ten Categories) has been the international standard since 1974. Each country runs its own registry, its own card, and its own rules.
Models: USA, corporate celebrity heroes. France and the EU, state-employed Graded, privacy laws, rank secrecy. Nigeria, Nollywood fame, private security, and weak state control. China, conscription. Russia, state ownership and organized crime. Japan and South Korea, idol agencies and ranking exams. Brazil and Mexico, Graded in militias and cartels. Gulf states, imported foreign Graded on exploitative contracts.
Distribution: Graded are spread roughly evenly by population, but the strongest are pulled toward rich countries. Africa, South Asia, and Latin America lose many B- and A-Ranks every year to recruiters from the US, Gulf, and Europe: the "rank drain."
Travel: B-Rank and above need a Halden travel endorsement; S and above need approval from both governments. SPA Graded are barred from most international flights. Refugee Graded are a political flashpoint everywhere.

94.content:
[GRADED: The Halden Commission]
A UN body created by the 1974 Halden Accords and headquartered in Geneva. It keeps the Strategic Registry (every S-Rank and above on Earth, with location tracking), sends inspectors to verify that no country is building a Graded army beyond treaty limits, and guards Halcyon's facility with a rotating international S-Rank detail.
Powerless in practice. The big powers ignore it when convenient, poor countries resent its inspections, and its inspectors are bribed, threatened, or killed. Still, an S-Rank who drops off the Registry triggers alarms in every capital, and Halden inspectors have real authority at borders.
Commission staff are often Graded from small neutral countries (Ireland, Costa Rica, Botswana, New Zealand), and their badge is a pale blue ring with the letters F to X around it.

95.content:
[GRADED: Interpol ECU]
Interpol's Enhanced Crimes Unit, based in Lyon, France, since 1979. It coordinates the hunt for Graded who cross borders: mercenaries, smugglers, terrorists, and S-Ranks who go missing from the Registry. It issues "violet notices" for wanted Graded (a variant of the red notice) and keeps the world's largest database of known powers, rank histories, and Strain signatures.
ECU agents have no arrest powers of their own. They work through local police, which in some countries means through people the target has already paid. Its Sniffers and PER analysts are among the best in the world.
Most-wanted list in 2026: Proxy (stateless SS PSI); "Mistral" (a French A-Rank SPA smuggler); and the unknown leadership of the Tontine.

96.content:
[GRADED: The Tontine]
A transnational criminal network that started in the 1970s among West African and French migrant savings circles (tontines) in Paris and Marseille. It grew into a financial and logistics syndicate moving money, people, and Graded between West Africa, France, and the Gulf.
Business: laundering mercenary payments; smuggling Graded across borders (SPA couriers, forged Halden endorsements); brokering West African B- and A-Ranks to Gulf employers and European private security; and moving Rush from Marseille into the Sahel and back.
Structure: no single boss. A council of "treasurers" in Lagos, Abidjan, Dakar, Paris, Marseille, and Dubai, each of whom pays into a shared pot and draws from it in turn, as in a real tontine. Betraying the circle means the circle stops paying, and then someone comes to collect.
Its people are polite, well dressed, and patient. It has done business with the Choir in Port Harlan and with French intelligence.

97.content:
[GRADED: Nigeria]
Registry: the National Enhanced Persons Commission (NEPC), founded 1963. Card: the green-and-white "NEPC card." Registration is mandatory but enforcement is patchy; an estimated 30% of Nigerian Graded are unregistered, and an NEPC card can be bought, lost, or "settled."
Population: about 45,000 registered Graded, the most in Africa. Nigeria's SS-Rank is HARMATTAN (Ifeyinwa Obiorah, 58, KIN, dust and wind; can black out the sky over a whole state). She is a national icon with a complicated relationship with every government since 1990, and she lives in Abuja under a Halden detail.
Graded life: Nollywood loves Graded stars, and B-Rank actors play themselves in hit films. Wealthy families, oil companies, banks, and politicians hire Graded bodyguards. Police have the Special Enhanced Response Squad (SERS), notorious for extortion and brutality; the #EndSERS protests of 2020 ended in the Lekki shootings. Prosperity megachurches feature BIO "miracle healers," some real, many not. The Graded rank drain to the US, UK, and Gulf is huge.
Slang: Graded are "powerman" or "powerwoman"; Duds are "spark-spark"; baselines are "ordinary people."

98.content:
[GRADED: Nigeria Through the Decades]
- 1960: Independence. The British colonial "Native Enhanced Register," which conscripted Graded into colonial police and mines, is abolished; the NEPC follows in 1963.
- 1967-70: The Nigerian Civil War. Both the federal army and Biafra field Graded units. Biafra's few Graded are famous for running supplies through the blockade (SPA couriers) and for the healers who worked themselves to death in the famine. The war's Graded veterans go unacknowledged for decades.
- 1970s: The oil boom. Oil companies hire Graded for pipelines, rigs, and security. Lagos explodes in size. Afrobeat-era nightlife features Graded performers.
- 1980s-1990s: Military governments use Graded enforcers against journalists and protesters. Harmattan Kindles in 1984 and is ranked SS in 1990; she refuses to serve the junta, and is placed under house arrest until 1998.
- 1999: Return to civilian rule. Nollywood booms through the 2000s with Graded hero films on VHS and VCD.
- 2010s-2020s: Insurgency in the north, with Graded fighters on several sides. Yaba's tech scene makes TEC Graded rich. #EndSERS (2020).
Money: naira. 1980s: ₦1 roughly matched $1. 2026: about ₦1,500 per dollar; a Lagos mainland room ₦300k-600k a year; a D-Rank security guard ₦150k-250k a month.

99.content:
[GRADED: Lagos]
Africa's biggest city, about 22 million people and roughly 9,000 registered Graded (and many more unregistered). Loud, fast, broke and rich at the same time, and running on hustle.
Districts:
- VICTORIA ISLAND and IKOYI: glass towers, embassies, oil money, Graded celebrities and their bodyguards, Ọ̀ṣọ́ Security's headquarters.
- LEKKI: new-money estates on reclaimed land; the Lekki toll gate, site of the 2020 shootings.
- LAGOS ISLAND and BALOGUN MARKET: the commercial heart. Graded porters, MAT traders "fixing" goods, pickpockets with E-Rank tricks.
- YABA: universities and the tech hub. TEC Graded, hacker crews, startup money.
- SURULERE and IKEJA: the middle-class mainland, with Nollywood studios and the NEPC Lagos office.
- AJEGUNLE and OSHODI: crowded, poor, tough. Area boys and motor-park agberos with Graded muscle.
- MAKOKO: a fishing community on stilts in the lagoon, home to many Duds and unregistered Graded, under constant threat of demolition.
Getting around: the go-slow (traffic) is endless. Danfo buses, okadas, the Third Mainland Bridge. SPA couriers charge a fortune to skip the traffic.
Power cuts are constant ("NEPA took light"); KIN electric Graded can earn more powering generators than in any other job.

100.content:
[GRADED: Lagos Powers]
Ọ̀ṢỌ́ SECURITY: the biggest private Graded security firm in West Africa. It guards banks, oil executives, politicians, and Nollywood stars, and runs its own rapid-response units, because "police no dey come." Its face is THUNDERBIRD (Kelechi Umeh, 33, B-III KIN electric), a Nollywood star who plays heroes on screen and mostly guards weddings in real life. Owner: Chief Adeolu Fadipe (64, baseline), politically connected and ruthless.
THE MOTOR PARK UNION: controls the bus parks and the street-level "settlement" economy. Mainland boss: ALHAJI TAJUDEEN "IRON TAJU" OGUNLESI (51, C-IV COR durability), smiling, generous, and dangerous. Runs area boys, protection, and votes.
LIVING FIRE MINISTRIES: a megachurch in Ikeja led by PASTOR EMEKA EZENWA (47, D-Rank BIO, a weak but genuine healer who stages miracles far bigger than his power). Huge congregation, private jet, ties to the Tontine.
THE COMPOUND: a Yaba collective of TEC Graded hackers. Some run startups, some run fraud, most do both.
NEPC LAGOS: Director HADIZA BELLO-KURFI (49, baseline), incorruptible and outgunned.
SERS (police Enhanced Response): checkpoints, extortion, and "settlement." Avoided by everyone.

101.content:
[GRADED: Ghana]
Registry: the Ghana Enhanced Persons Registry (1958), the first in independent Africa. Card: red, gold, and green with a black star.
History: after independence in 1957, Ghana's government founded the African Personality Corps (1960-66), a Pan-African program inviting Graded from across the continent to train in Accra and serve liberation movements. It was disbanded after the 1966 coup, and its veterans scattered across Africa, some into politics and some into mercenary work. Graded Kumasi goldsmiths (MAT) are famous.
Today: a stable democracy with relatively liberal Graded laws, no public rank display, and strong anti-discrimination courts. Accra is a hub for Graded tech, music, and returning diaspora Graded escaping US and UK rank discrimination. It's also a Tontine transit point.
Accra: Osu (nightlife), Jamestown (old fishing quarter, boxing gyms full of Graded kids), Airport City (money), Makola Market.

102.content:
[GRADED: Francophone West Africa]
Most countries kept French-style law after independence: Graded registries modeled on France's, rank secrecy on paper, and close ties with French security services.
FRANÇAFRIQUE: France has kept deploying Graded in its former colonies: as "advisers," as presidential guards, and in military operations in the Sahel (2013-2022). Many West Africans resent French Graded on their soil, and anti-French protests in Bamako, Ouagadougou, and Niamey target them.
SENEGAL: stable and proud. Dakar is a hub for music, wrestling (lutte, with a famous Graded division), fishing, and migration. Graded wrestlers are national celebrities.
CÔTE D'IVOIRE: civil wars in 2002-2007 and 2010-2011, with Graded fighters on both sides. Abidjan is booming, Plateau's towers are full of business, and Yopougon's nightlife is full of Graded performers.
THE SAHEL: insurgencies, coups (2020-2023), and Graded fighters from every side, including foreign mercenaries.
Money: CFA franc. 103.content:
[GRADED: The Mano River Wars (1989-2003)]
The civil wars in Liberia and Sierra Leone were among the worst Graded conflicts on Earth. Warlords forcibly recruited Kindled teenagers, kept them fighting with crude Ichor-cut stimulants (a precursor of Rush), and used MAT Graded to work the diamond fields. ECOMOG, the West African peacekeeping force led by Nigeria, sent its own Graded units in; some were heroes, some were as bad as the warlords.
Aftermath: thousands of former Graded child fighters, many unregistered and many with permanent Strain damage, grew up without schooling, family, or treatment. Some are now community leaders, some mercenaries, some in the Tontine. Truth commissions documented it all, and almost nobody was punished.
Handle this history with weight: survivors are real people in-story, not set dressing.

104.content:
[GRADED: France]
Registry: the Direction Générale des Personnes Augmentées (DGPA), founded 1959, part of the Interior Ministry. Card: the "carte de classification," kept private.
LE SECRET DU RANG (1981): asking anyone their rank is illegal, for employers, landlords, police without a warrant, and private individuals in a commercial setting. No public rank display. In theory, France doesn't see rank. In practice, everyone guesses, and discrimination is quieter but real, especially for Graded from the banlieues and from immigrant families.
HEROES ARE CIVIL SERVANTS: there are no corporate heroes, since the EU bans hero branding. Licensed Graded join the Corps des Agents Augmentés (CAA), with a salary, a pension, ranks, paperwork, and a union. CAA heroes go on strike, famously in 1995 and 2019, and Paris burns a little more each time. Police have augmented units (BRI-A in Paris).
LA LÉGION: the Foreign Legion's 1er Régiment Étranger Augmenté takes Graded from anywhere, no questions asked, and grants French citizenship after service. Many West African, Eastern European, and Latin American Graded have come to France this way.
Politics: the far-right Front Humain campaigns on "baseline France first." Population: about 14,000 registered Graded; no SS-Rank; 9 S-Ranks.

105.content:
[GRADED: France Through the Decades]
- 1954-62: The Algerian War. France deploys Graded paratroopers, and PSI interrogators are used in the Battle of Algiers (1957), part of the torture scandal that haunts France for decades. Algerian Graded fight for independence; many families who came to France afterward carry that history.
- 1959: The DGPA is founded.
- MAY '68: Students and workers paralyze France. Graded students hold the barricades in the Latin Quarter, and a young KIN student's "wall of fire" photo becomes iconic. Graded rights become a cause of the French left.
- 1981: Le secret du rang becomes law.
- 1980s-90s: Banlieue estates fill with immigrant families, Graded and baseline. The CAA strike of 1995 shuts the country down alongside the general strikes. France wins the 1998 World Cup with an all-baseline team, under rules that ban Graded players.
- 2002: The franc becomes the euro.
- 2005: The banlieue riots. Augmented units patrol the cités; Graded youth form crews like the Sans-Rang.
- 2010s-2020s: Sahel operations, the rise of Front Humain, CAA strikes in 2019, and the Paris 2024 Olympics, which exclude Graded (and set off protests across the banlieues).

106.content:
[GRADED: Paris]
About 12 million in the metro area and 3,800 registered Graded.
- CENTRAL PARIS (Le Marais, the Latin Quarter, Saint-Germain): rich, beautiful, and policed. The Graded here are civil servants, academics, and the discreet rich who never mention their rank.
- LA DÉFENSE: the business district. Corporate security firms legally employ Graded as "agents de sécurité," a loophole around the hero-branding ban.
- BELLEVILLE and BARBÈS: working-class, multicultural, North and West African, Chinese, and Graded-friendly. Underground Graded bars, illegal rank-reveal nights, Tontine savings circles in back rooms.
- PIGALLE: nightlife and sex work; Graded performers and bouncers.
- THE CATACOMBS: 300 km of tunnels under the city, used by Graded smugglers, raves, cults, and anyone who wants to avoid the BRI-A.
- SEINE-SAINT-DENIS ("the 93"): tower-block cités (Clichy-sous-Bois, Saint-Denis, Bobigny). Young, poor, heavily policed, with a high rate of unregistered Graded. Home of the Sans-Rang.
The périphérique ring road is the line between Paris and everything else, and everyone knows which side they're from.

107.content:
[GRADED: Paris Powers]
BRI-A: the Paris police's augmented intervention brigade. Chief: COMMISSAIRE ODILE BRASSAC (55, B-V SPA, local gravity; the officer who makes riot shields bend). Cold, by-the-book, and privately disgusted with what her brigade does in the banlieues.
THE CAA: the hero civil service. Its most famous agent and union leader is BASTILLE (Gwenaëlle Le Floch, 44, A-III COR, a Breton dockworker's daughter). She will strike, march, and punch a minister on camera, and the public loves her for it.
THE SANS-RANG: a loose network of banlieue youth who refuse registration or refuse to reveal their rank. Some are activists, some are a gang, most are both. They have no leader on paper; in practice everyone listens to LE FANTÔME DE BARBÈS (Moussa Diakhaté, 29, B-IV SPA, phasing), a vigilante the police have never managed to hold.
FRONT HUMAIN: the far-right "baseline France first" party, polling at 25%.
DGPA: Director THIERRY VALADIER (58, baseline), a smooth technocrat who believes in rank secrecy and also keeps secret files on every Graded in the country.
Wanted: MISTRAL (identity unknown, A-Rank SPA), a smuggler who moves people and goods between Marseille, Paris, and North Africa for the Tontine.

108.content:
[GRADED: Marseille]
France's great port city, with about 1.8 million people and 1,600 registered Graded. Sun, mistral wind, football, fish soup, and the drug trade.
- VIEUX-PORT and LE PANIER: the old harbor and the oldest quarter, tourist cafés over smugglers' cellars.
- THE QUARTIERS NORD: poor northern estates where the drug points ("points de deal") run day and night. Gangs fight over them with Graded enforcers, and the body count makes national news every summer.
- THE PORT: containers from North Africa, Asia, and West Africa. Rush comes in here and goes out to Paris, Spain, and the Sahel.
- THE CALANQUES: cliffs and coves where Graded smugglers land boats at night.
The old Corsican-Marseille underworld (the milieu) has used Graded since the 1950s; the French Connection heroin trade of the 1960s-70s used SPA couriers. Today the milieu, the Quartiers Nord gangs, and the Tontine share the city uneasily. Marseille's police augmented unit is underfunded and outgunned, and everyone knows it.

109.content:
[GRADED: United Kingdom]
Registry: the Home Office Enhanced Persons Directorate (1950). Card: a plain grey "EP card" with the rank shown as a number (1 for F up to 7 for S), never a color. "What number are you?" is a deeply rude question asked constantly.
Class and rank: the British class system absorbed rank. Graded from posh families go to Oxford and into the civil service; working-class Graded go into the army, the Met's SO-E augmented unit, or crime. Tabloids are obsessed with Graded scandals. A royal cousin's Kindling in 1986 was hushed up for years.
History: Graded in the Falklands (1982); the Troubles in Northern Ireland, with Graded on several sides; football hooligan firms with Graded members in the '80s; a booming London Graded club scene in the '90s.
London: the City (money and private Graded security), Peckham and Brixton (multicultural, a big West African Graded diaspora), Canary Wharf, council estates in the outer boroughs.

110.content:
[GRADED: Germany and Central Europe]
GERMANY: the strictest privacy laws in Europe. The Bundesamt für Erweiterte Personen (BEP) holds rank data under heavy protection; using someone's rank against them is a crime. The Bundeswehr may not deploy Graded abroad except under UN mandate. Graded work mostly as engineers, rescuers, and police (GSG-E).
History: the Nazi regime ended in 1945, before the first Kindling, but fear of "selection" shapes German Graded law to this day. East Germany's Stasi ran ABTEILUNG P, a Graded secret-police unit whose files (opened in 1992) showed decades of PSI surveillance; its refusal to act in 1989 helped bring down the Wall. Berlin's 1990s techno scene was full of Graded DJs and illegal clubs in abandoned bunkers.
POLAND and the former Eastern Bloc: Soviet-era Graded programs left veterans and files everywhere. Since 2004, many Eastern European Graded have moved west for work, and their rank-based wages are a political argument in every election.
Money: Deutsche Mark until 2002, then the euro.

111.content:
[GRADED: Russia]
Registry: the Federal Service for Enhanced Persons (FSEL), successor to the Soviet Directorate S. Every Graded of C-Rank and above must serve the state for five years, in the army, the security services, or "penal battalions" for those convicted of crimes.
1990s: when the USSR collapsed, thousands of Graded were left unpaid and armed. They became bodyguards, enforcers, and Bratva "brothers," and the Loose Graded crisis gave Moscow's '90s their reputation. Graded oligarch bodyguards are still a status symbol.
GRAPHITE (Pyotr Zhukov), Russia's SS-Rank since Chernobyl, lives in a guarded zone near Moscow and appears only at state occasions. Russia lost its second SS, Proxy, in 2017, which is a source of enormous embarrassment.
Wars: Graded units fought in Afghanistan (1979-89), Chechnya (1994-96, 1999-2009), and Ukraine (2014 onward), where Graded fight on both sides and Halden inspectors are routinely ignored.

112.content:
[GRADED: China]
Registry: the Ministry of Enhanced Affairs, with nationwide testing at birth, 12, and 15. Every Graded of B-Rank and above is conscripted for at least 10 years: the military, state industry, or state security. Rank is recorded in every citizen's social file.
TIANJIAN GROUP: the state-owned conglomerate that employs most Graded outside the military, in construction (MAT), the power grid (KIN), logistics (SPA), and surveillance (PER, TEC). China's megaprojects of the 1990s-2010s were built partly by Graded labor brigades.
China has two SS-Ranks, both entirely state-controlled: KUNLUN (MAT, mountains and earthquakes) and TIDEWALL (KIN, water and pressure). Neither has appeared in public since 2015.
Graded life: a stable state career with good pay and no freedom. Low-rank Graded are often pushed into factory or rural work. Hong Kong had its own registry until 1997, and a looser one afterward until 2020.

113.content:
[GRADED: Japan and South Korea]
JAPAN: Graded talent agencies run heroes like idols, with strict image rules, dating bans, managed fan clubs, handshake events, and burnout. Rank-exam cram schools (juku) prepare marker-positive kids for Assessment. Yakuza families recruited Graded heavily in the bubble era of the 1980s. Many Duds become hikikomori. The 1995 Kobe earthquake made Graded rescuers national heroes. Registry: the Enhanced Persons Agency (1954).
SOUTH KOREA: the most rank-obsessed country on Earth. The annual Graded suneung assessment can decide a teenager's entire future; hagwon cram schools run until midnight. Chaebol conglomerates sponsor hero teams. All Graded men serve two years in the military's augmented units, and women can volunteer. K-drama and K-pop have Graded stars, and hiding your rank in the entertainment industry is common. Registry: the Ministry of Enhanced Persons (1961), shaped by the Korean War, in which Graded fought on both sides.

114.content:
[GRADED: India and South Asia]
1947, the same year as the Halcyon Event, was the year of Partition. The first Graded in South Asia Kindled in the middle of that violence, and their stories are still told on both sides of the border.
INDIA: the National Enhanced Persons Bureau (1952) runs a mixed system: public-sector jobs, the army, and a huge private sector. Bollywood has made Graded heroes a film genre since the 1970s. Rank, caste, class, and religion overlap in complicated ways, and Graded from marginalized communities face prejudice on both counts; high rank can also break old barriers. India's SS-Rank is SAHYADRI (Aruna Kulkarni, 49, MAT, mountains and stone), who rebuilt Gujarat after the 2001 earthquake. Rank drain to the Gulf, UK, and US is massive, and IT companies hire TEC Graded in Bengaluru.
PAKISTAN and BANGLADESH: their own registries since 1948 and 1972. India and Pakistan's Graded border units are a constant source of tension, and Halden inspectors watch them closely.
Mumbai: Bandra (film money), Dharavi (enterprise, poverty, Graded workshops), Colaba, and the train network where SPA Graded are banned from the carriages.

115.content:
[GRADED: Latin America]
BRAZIL: the military dictatorship (1964-85) used Graded in its repression, and democracy brought a truth commission and little justice. Favelas are contested by gangs and milícias (militias of off-duty police), both full of Graded. Carnival features Graded samba schools. Brazil's SS-Rank is POROROCA (Jefferson Amaral da Cunha, 61, MAT, water; named after the Amazon's tidal bore), a beloved former footballer who Kindled at 30, forcing his retirement from the game. São Paulo and Rio have huge private security industries.
MEXICO: the cartels field more Graded than some armies, as sicarios, smugglers, and tunnel diggers (MAT). The government's Graded units are infiltrated. Mexico City has a vibrant Graded arts and lucha libre scene (the Graded lucha league is one of the most-watched sports in the country).
COLOMBIA: the Medellín and Cali cartels of the '80s and '90s used Graded hitmen and bodyguards; peace in 2016 left many former Graded guerrillas without a place.
CUBA: a state Graded program with famous doctors and healers sent abroad on medical missions.

116.content:
[GRADED: Middle East and North Africa]
THE GULF: the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar are short on homegrown Graded and buy foreign ones: West African, South Asian, and Eastern European Graded work security, construction, cooling (KIN), and desalination (MAT) on sponsorship contracts where employers hold their passports. Wages are high and conditions can be brutal. Dubai's towers were partly raised by Graded labor; Graded bodyguards are a status symbol for the rich.
NORTH AFRICA: Algeria's Graded fought France for independence (1954-62). Morocco, Algeria, and Tunisia have strict registries and close (often uneasy) ties to France. Many families in the Paris banlieues and Marseille have roots here, and the smuggling routes run both ways across the Mediterranean.
EGYPT: the Arab Spring of 2011 saw Graded protesters in Tahrir Square; the security state that followed keeps tight control of Graded.
TURKEY and IRAN: regional powers with conscripted Graded corps and their own S-Ranks under Halden watch.

117.content:
[GRADED: East and Southern Africa]
SOUTH AFRICA: under apartheid, the "Enhanced Persons Registration Act" of 1952 layered rank onto racial classification: Black Graded were conscripted into mine labor or banned outright, while white Graded served the security forces. Graded fought in the liberation struggle, from the townships to exile training camps, and the 1976 Soweto uprising included Graded students. After 1994, a Truth and Reconciliation process heard Graded testimony from both sides. Today Johannesburg has a booming Graded private security industry (the largest in the world per capita), a Graded mining scene, and deep inequality.
KENYA: Nairobi is East Africa's tech and media hub. Graded are banned from athletics, so every Kenyan distance champion is suspected of hiding a Kindling. The Graded matatu (minibus) crews are famous for speed.
ETHIOPIA: a proud Graded military tradition; Addis Ababa hosts the African Union's Graded affairs office.
The rank drain hits the whole region hard: much of its trained Graded talent ends up in the Gulf or Europe.
